amendments.rule: Where English fuses several morphemes into one word, such as *wherein*, they share a unit **only when that shared English rendering carries the sense of every morpheme placed in it**. Reserve `added` for English that no morpheme licenses at all. This governs a fixed multi-word Hebrew expression the ASV renders with one English word too, but it never absorbs a morpheme whose sense that rendering does not carry: in `דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים` → *chronicles*, the two lexical nouns may share *chronicles*, while the separately segmented article takes a written *the* or is its own `unrepresented` unit; `אִם לֹא` → *surely* may share one unit when *surely* carries both morphemes' senses. Such a fused expression is headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme, rather than leaving another morpheme whose sense the rendering carries `unrepresented`. The one-English-word condition is load-bearing in both directions: `בְּיַד` → *by* and `מִפְּנֵי` → *because of* fuse, but where the ASV spends a second English word on the expression — `הֵשִׁיב פָּנִים` → *deny* fuses while the same idiom as *say ... nay* does not — the condition is unmet and rule 2 splits it. **Read that condition as one English rendering, not one English token.** A compound English preposition written in two or three words — *because of*, *by reason of*, *out of* — is a single rendering of which no morpheme owns a part, and it fuses; so does an expression whose unit additionally carries a copula or other word the construction hands to the whole of it under another rule, as `לִפְנֵי` → *was before*. What defeats the condition is English the ASV spends on one morpheme in particular, so that each morpheme has a rendering of its own: `לִפְנֵי` → *to meet* gives *to* to the preposition and *meet* to `פָּנֶה`, and `עַד לְ` → *until there was* gives *until* to `עַד` and the predicate's supplied copula to the `לְ` under rule 49, while the same `עַד לְ` → *to* fuses. Test by subtraction as rules 16 and 31 do: drop the second English word and ask whether a particular morpheme has lost its rendering or only the expression as a whole is diminished. What the second morpheme is tagged does not matter; a preposition before a construct noun fuses on the same terms as a compound preposition. **And such a compound's single English word carries the preposition's own relation even where no part of it states that relation separately.** Where `מִן`, `לְ`, `בְּ` or `עַל` stands before a construct noun and the ASV writes one English preposition for the pair, the condition is met and the two share a unit headed on the construct noun: `מִפְּנֵי` → *before*, `לִפְנֵי` → *before*, `עַל־פְּנֵי` → *upon*, `בְּקֶרֶב` → *among*. **Read that list as the commonest prepositions and not as a closed one:** what licenses the fusion is that a preposition stands on a construct noun and one English rendering carries the pair, so a `כְּ`, an `אֶל`, an `אַחַר` or any other preposition in that position is read on exactly the same terms, and `כְּפִי` → *as* fuses as `לְפִי` and `מִפְּנֵי` do. Do not read this rule's first sentence as requiring a separate English trace of the ablative, directional or locative sense before fusing, and do not mark the preposition `unrepresented` beside a construct noun holding the whole word: that is the outcome the fusion sentence above forbids and the one rule 22's closing paragraph forbids for a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a word, and the subtraction test finds no second English word for either morpheme to own. **The same prohibition runs the other way, and the construct noun is the side more often mistaken.** Do not mark the construct noun `unrepresented` beside a preposition holding the whole rendering either: the noun of such a compound is not a word the ASV ever writes alone, its sense is inside the one English word exactly as the preposition's is, and the reasoning that forbids the one direction forbids the other, so the two share a unit headed on the construct noun as before. Read whether any English word in the expression renders that noun's own lexeme, which is this rule's subtraction test again: `כְּפִיךָ` → *even as* ... *art* writes nothing for `פֶּה` in particular, so the pair fuses and the suffix keeps only the *thou* rule 18 writes for it, while `לִפְנֵי` → *to meet* gives `פָּנֶה` a word of its own and rule 2 splits it. A pronominal suffix on the construct noun is no part of the fusion in either case: it takes whatever English pronoun the ASV writes for it under rule 18, or goes `unrepresented` under rule 40 where the ASV writes none, and its presence is not evidence that the preposition and its noun have separate renderings. Where the ASV instead writes a word for each — `מִפְּנֵי` → *from before*, `מִקֶּרֶב` → *from among* — each morpheme has a rendering of its own, the condition is unmet, and rule 2 splits them; what tells the two shapes apart is independently recoverable ownership under rule 2, not the raw number of English words or which senses an English preposition leaves implicit. The corpus fuses `מִפְּנֵי` to *before* in fifteen units and to *because of* in seventy-five, `לִפְנֵי` to *before* in five hundred and ninety-seven, and a preposition with `תּוֹךְ` or `קֶרֶב` to *among* in twenty-seven. Contiguity is part of the condition for such an expression: a verb and the preposition it governs, held apart by the subject or the object, is not one. It is not a condition on fusion generally — rule 35's *Nor* and *never* fuse across intervening material, because there the one English word still carries every morpheme's sense. `גָּדַל ... מִן` → *exceeded* and `הוֹסִיף ... אֶל` → *exceed* are a verb whose preposition the ASV's comparative recasting leaves unrendered, so rule 2 splits them and the preposition is `unrepresented`. Rule 22 governs a repetition of the *same* element, not the parts of an idiom. **The expression need not be an idiom, and a full lexical noun fuses on the same terms as a function morpheme.** Where Hebrew writes a generic head noun before an attributive that names the class — `אִשָּׁה` or `אִישׁ` before a participle or an adjective — and the ASV renders the pair by one English word, the two share one unit headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme: `אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה` → *harlot's* is one unit headed on `זוֹנָה`, with the indefinite article going to that nominal expression under rule 15, and `אִשָּׁה` is not marked `unrepresented` beside it. The one-English-word condition and its subtraction test decide this exactly as they decide a compound preposition — dropping the English word diminishes only the expression as a whole, and no morpheme owns a part of it — so where the ASV instead spends a word on each, as `אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה` → *man of war*, the condition is unmet and rule 2 splits it. Do not read *fixed multi-word Hebrew expression* above as a requirement that the pair be idiomatic. **For this rule, a particle's single idiomatic English rendering includes the pronouns the English formula requires.** The entreaty particle `נָא` → *I beseech thee* or *we pray thee* takes the complete formula, headed on *beseech* or *pray*; its English subject and object pronouns are not `added`, because they realize the particle's one entreaty rather than supply arguments of the neighbouring imperative. Where the ASV's formula omits an object, as *I pray*, align only what it writes.
amendments.why: Job 33 analysed the same construction two ways in adjacent verses: 33.5 fused lə + pānay as one unit headed on the construct noun, while 33.6 gave the whole of *even as ... art* to kə and marked pî unrepresented. Rule 30 already forbids the mirror error — leaving the preposition unrepresented beside a construct noun holding the word — but says nothing in terms about leaving the construct noun unrepresented beside a preposition holding it, and its example list reads as though restricted to min, lə, bə and al, none of which is kə. Those two gaps are exactly what the verse pass fell through, so the correction belongs in rule 30's own text rather than in a new rule pointing back at it. The additions are the symmetry, the statement that the preposition list is open (which the rule's own 'what the second morpheme is tagged does not matter' already implies), and the ruling that a suffix on the construct noun is no part of the fusion and no evidence against it — the shape both Job 33.5 and 33.6 have. Nothing in the corpus contradicts: the lə table shows liphnê fused in 424 aligned and 265 noncompositional units, the min table shows mippenê and mê'êth fused, and no row shows a construct noun of such a compound left unrepresented beside its preposition. The rest of the rule, including the one-rendering paragraph, the contiguity carve-out, the lexical-noun paragraph and the nā formula sentence, is reproduced unchanged.

conventions: A preposition standing on a construct noun that the ASV renders by one English relational expression is fused into a single noncompositional unit headed on the construct noun, with any pronominal suffix keeping its own English pronoun as a separate unit. The chapter reads lə + pānay -> 'before' (33.5) and kə + pî -> 'even as ... art' (33.6) alike; the construct noun is never marked unrepresented beside a preposition holding the whole rendering.

Where a waw whose clause the ASV recasts as subordinate is rendered by the pair 'So that', the unit is headed on the coordinator 'So' (33.20, 33.26). Rule 55 leaves this head a genuine choice and the corpus heads such pairs both ways; the chapter took the coordinator throughout.

report: One real cross-verse split. JOB.33.5 fuses lə + pānay into one noncompositional unit for *before*, headed on the construct noun (rules 30 and 23), with the suffix taking its own *me*. JOB.33.6 took the same shape — kə + pî + kā — and gave the whole of *even as ... art* to the preposition while marking pî unrepresented. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: both are a preposition standing on a construct body-part noun that together render as a single English relational expression, with the suffix separately realized. Patched JOB.33.6 to the verse-5 analysis.

The subtraction test decides it: none of *even*, *as* or *art* renders peh's lexeme in particular, so no morpheme owns a part of the expression and rule 30's one-rendering condition holds. The old unit left a lexical noun with no English at all standing beside a preposition that held the whole rendering, which is the outcome rule 30's fusion sentence and rule 22's closing paragraph both forbid — stated there only in the mirror direction, which is why the verse pass fell into it.

BSB's eight disagreements: JOB.33.6 pî is the genuine one and is corrected here. The other seven are documented convention differences and not errors — paragogic he at 33.1 and 33.5 (twice) under rule 32; lə at 33.10 recast as a possessive determiner on the noun beside it, bə at 33.16 and bā at 33.28 with their objects promoted to direct objects, all under rule 40; and the unrendered object suffix at 33.20 under rule 22. No accepted edge was changed to improve the aggregate.

Cleared as context-licensed rather than split: shachath takes a supplied *the* only where no article morpheme stands (33.18, 33.24, 33.30) and leaves the written *the* to the article where one does (33.22, 33.28); min's five renderings track comparative, privative, partitive and ablative uses; the article is represented exactly where the ASV writes a *the* (33.6 against 33.11 and 33.18); and the waw's *Then*, *and*, *So that*, *Yea*, *also* and *And* are each read off the ASV with a waw present, against the added *yea* of 33.29 where no conjunction morpheme stands.

Cleared on structure: supplied prepositions before bare nominals are uniformly rule 33 (33.12, 33.15, 33.17, 33.19, 33.24) and verb-valency prepositions uniformly rule 44 (33.1, 33.13, 33.24, 33.26); supplied relatives join the noun where the ASV recasts a nominal (33.3, 33.23, 33.27, 33.32) and are added at 33.21, where the Hebrew writes the antecedent and juxtaposes a finite clause, which is the boundary rule 46 draws in its own terms. Light-verb heads and phrasal-particle heads agree across all fourteen instances.

Both textual decisions were left as the projection carries them (rule 9): the selected readings at 33.19 and 33.28, and the underdetermined unit at 33.21 resolved to r00-base, which the ASV's rendering permits. No unit is rule 53's case.
